Still, Northmere had enough. They were all out for 176 in the forty-fifth over, and the total felt modest only if read without context. Read properly, it had a long second-wicket base, a captain’s seventy, a late lower-order scrape, and nineteen extras that Southbay would later regret not because they looked enormous on their own, but because the final margin left no room for generosity.

Good afternoon from Southbank Oval in Fairhaven, where Fairmont chose to bat and ended up producing the kind of innings that feels ordinary only if you glance at the final total too quickly, because their 318 all out was not built in one smooth climb but in a set of sharply different phases: a controlled start, a quick captain’s lift, a long middle repair, and then a late burst so violent that Westmere were left chasing not just a large score but the emotional damage of having watched the innings get away after they had created several chances to pull it back.
